{{One source|date=January 2024}}

[[File:Nara Sudo-tenno-sha.jpg|280px|thumb|Sudo Tenno Shrine, Nishikidera-cho, Nara City]]
'''Sudo Tenno Shrine''' (崇道天皇神社, ''Sudō Tennō Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} primarily dedicated to {{ill|Prince Sawara|en|Prince Sawara|qid=Q1079634|lt=Prince Sawara}} (Emperor Sudo), found primarily in Nara and across Western Japan{{sfn|小さき社の列島史|p=89}}. Alternative names include '''Sudō Tennō-sha''' (崇道天皇社), '''Sudō Jinja''' (崇道神社), and phonetic variations such as '''Sōdō Jinja''' (宗道神社) or '''Sōdo Jinja''' (惣戸神社){{sfn|小さき社の列島史|p=89}}.

== History ==
This shrine venerates {{ill|Prince Sawara|en|Prince Sawara|qid=Q1079634|lt=Prince Sawara}}, who died under suspicion of involvement in the assassination of {{ill|Fujiwara no Tanetsugu|en|Fujiwara no Tanetsugu|qid=Q3090668|lt=Fujiwara no Tanetsugu}}. He passed away during exile in {{ill|Awaji Province|en|Awaji Province|qid=Q1053717|lt=Awaji Province}}, and later was believed to cause calamities. Thus, the shrine has a strong association with the {{ill|Goryō|en|Goryō|qid=Q3273210|lt=Goryō faith}}. Prince Sawara was reburied at {{ill|Yashima Mausoleum|ja|八島陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yashima Tomb|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q24875285}} in Yamato Province, where a shrine named {{ill|Yashima Mausoleum|ja|八島陵#崇道天皇社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sudō Tennō-sha (Yashima Tomb)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q24875285}} existed until 1886. Nearby smaller shrines are believed to have branched from it{{sfn|小さき社の列島史|p=127}}. The Sudō Tennō-sha in Nishikidera-cho, Nara City, is thought to be established on the former site of the mikoshi hall dedicated to Emperor Sudo during the Nanto Goryō-e (南都御霊会) rituals{{sfn|小さき社の列島史|p=126}}<ref>璉珹寺紀</ref><ref>{{ill|Murai Kodō|ja|奈良坊目拙解|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nara Bōmoku Sekkai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 村井古道|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q96711987}}</ref>.

In regional areas, particularly in the {{ill|San'yō region|en|San'yō region|qid=Q398087|lt=San'yō region}}, the Sudō Jinja or Sōdō shrines may originate from granaries built in 805 (Enryaku 24) by imperial order for the appeasement of Emperor Sudo’s spirit. These granaries later became shrines{{sfn|小さき社の列島史|p=120}}<ref name="koki">Nihon Kōki (日本後紀), Enryaku 24</ref><ref name="ruiju">Ruiju Sandai Kyaku (類従三代格)</ref>. These granaries stored 40 bundles of rice annually from each county to appease his spirit{{sfn|小さき社の列島史|p=120}}<ref name="koki"/><ref name="ruiju"/>{{sfn|小さき社の列島史|p=125}}<ref>Ōkagami</ref><ref>Daianji Sudō Tennō Miin Yashima Ryosho Kibun</ref>.

Some shrines named Sudō Jinja do not enshrine Prince Sawara. For instance, according to the Kōfukuji Kanmu Chōsho (興福寺官務牒疏, 1441), the Sudō Tennō Jinja in Haji, Sōraku County, {{ill|Yamashiro Province|en|Yamashiro Province|qid=Q749276|lt=Yamashiro Province}}, venerates {{ill|Prince Toneri|en|Prince Toneri|qid=Q1362200|lt=Prince Toneri}}<ref>Kōfukuji Kanmu Chōsho</ref>{{sfn|小さき社の列島史|p=127}}. This may be due to confusion stemming from Prince Toneri’s posthumous title, '''Sudō Jinkei Kōtei''' (崇道尽敬皇帝){{sfn|小さき社の列島史|p=127}}.
